children: is accelerating its AI infrastructure push, prompting Citi to sharply raise its capital-spending forecasts as the Chinese technology giant targets 20 gigawatts of AI capacity by 2032. The expanded investment carries substantial execution and spending risk, but Citi believes the buildout could turn Alibaba Cloud into a dramatically larger AI business, with external AI cloud revenue potentially reaching $168 billion by fiscal 2033.

Alibaba operates one of China's largest e-commerce ecosystems through platforms including Taobao and Tmall, while Alibaba Cloud provides computing, storage and AI infrastructure to businesses. The company increasingly views cloud and artificial intelligence as major long-term growth engines alongside its core commerce operations.

To support management's 20GW AI infrastructure target by 2032, we assume a 50/50 Capex/Opex partner split at US$30bn/1GW, raising our FY27FY29E capex forecasts to Rmb258bn, Rmb283bn, and Rmb282bn, Citi analyst Alicia Yap wrote.

Under Citi's assumptions, external AI cloud revenue could reach $168 billion by fiscal 2033, representing roughly 40% compound annual growth from fiscal 2026. Citi's sensitivity range stretches from $126 billion to $210 billion.
The technological push is also broadening. T-Head unveiled its Zhenwu V900 accelerator and Lingjun Supernode infrastructure to power AliCloud's production-ready agentic cloud platform, Yap said.

Alibaba is simultaneously expanding its Qwen model family, including the 2.4-trillion-parameter Qwen3.8-Max, while developing smaller models aimed at cheaper real-world deployment and expanding into image, audio and world models.
Citi reiterated its Buy rating and $190 price target.
Alibaba shares nevertheless fell 3.7% in premarket trading amid concerns surrounding a reported Chinese government probe, showing that regulatory risk can still overshadow improving AI fundamentals.
Alibaba's central investment question is whether enormous AI spending produces revenue quickly enough to justify the capital commitment.
Investors should watch cloud revenue growth, AI workload adoption, infrastructure utilization and capex returns as spending climbs toward Citi's RMB 258 billion to RMB 283 billion annual estimates.

The bullish case strengthens if external AI cloud revenue tracks toward Citi's 40% annual growth forecast. Slower monetization would make the scale of Alibaba's infrastructure ambitions considerably harder to justify, while Chinese regulatory developments remain an additional near-term risk for BABA shares.

title: Citi Doubles Down on Alibaba Stock as AI Ambitions Accelerate
